weights.weightCitation: ESC 2022 Ventricular Arrhythmias & Sudden Cardiac Death Guideline (Zeppenfeld K et al.); Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022). REGULAR FAST palpitations WITH SYNCOPE/presyncope or chest pain in someone with structural heart disease (IHD, HF, cardiomyopathy) or FHx sudden death is VT until proven otherwise. 12-lead ECG + urgent cardiology; syncope-WITH-palpitations is the cardinal red flag.

ESC 2024 Atrial Fibrillation Guideline (Van Gelder IC et al.); Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022). IRREGULARLY IRREGULAR fast palpitations; rate control + anticoagulation per stroke risk — but ANTICOAGULATE regardless in VALVULAR/rheumatic AF (see RHD entry); always seek a precipitant (thyrotoxicosis, sepsis, alcohol, PE).

ESC 2019 Supraventricular Tachycardia Guideline (Brugada J et al.); Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022). REGULAR, fast, ABRUPT onset AND offset (a 'switch'); often young; vagal manoeuvres/adenosine terminate it; WPW (delta wave) is a substrate — avoid AV-nodal blockers in pre-excited AF.

American Thyroid Association thyrotoxicosis guidance; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022). PERSISTENT palpitations + heat intolerance + weight loss (with preserved/increased appetite) + tremor; causes sinus tachycardia OR AF; check TFTs — a thyroid cause must be sought in new AF.

WHO anaemia guidance; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022). Compensatory sinus tachycardia from anaemia -> palpitations (worse on exertion) + pallor + fatigue; UGANDA causes — malaria, hookworm/iron-deficiency, sickle-cell, chronic disease; check FBC/Hb.

Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022) (ectopic beats / anxiety-related palpitations). Awareness of SINGLE skipped/extra beats (ectopics) or situational/anxiety-related palpitations WITHOUT syncope — usually benign; but palpitations WITH syncope are NEVER attributed to anxiety until a malignant arrhythmia is excluded.

weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL on rheumatic heart disease. UGANDA: RHD is a LEADING cause of AF in YOUNG adults (mitral valve disease -> AF) — distinct from the elderly hypertensive AF of the West. KEY MANAGEMENT difference: VALVULAR (rheumatic/mitral-stenosis) AF needs ANTICOAGULATION regardless of CHA2DS2-VASc, and WARFARIN (not DOACs) for mitral stenosis/mechanical valves; echo for valve assessment; secondary rheumatic prophylaxis. Overlaps 'AF with RVR' but flags the valvular aetiology.
weights.weightCitation: WHO rheumatic heart disease guidance; ESC valvular & AF guidelines; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022)

weights.dx: Sinus tachycardia secondary to systemic illness
weights.csoNote: The COMMONEST 'palpitations' at a Ugandan referral hospital — a reactive REGULAR SINUS tachycardia driven by a SYSTEMIC cause: FEVER/SEPSIS/MALARIA, dehydration, pain, anaemia, hypoxia, or thyrotoxicosis. The palpitations are a SYMPTOM — find and treat the cause (the rhythm itself is not the problem). Heart rate is in vitals; ECG shows sinus tachycardia.
weights.weightCitation: Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022) (sinus tachycardia secondary to systemic illness)

weights.csoNote: HYPOKALAEMIA/HYPOMAGNESAEMIA (from diarrhoea, vomiting, diuretics — common in Uganda) create an ARRHYTHMIA SUBSTRATE -> ectopics, and can precipitate VT/TORSADES (links to the VT and long-QT entries). The electrolyte VALUES (K, Mg) are lab-measured and NOT tokenised — recommend checking U&E/Mg in palpitations with these risks; ECG (U waves, long QT). Correct K AND Mg together.
weights.weightCitation: Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022) (hypokalaemia/hypomagnesaemia and arrhythmia)

weights.csoNote: Drug/stimulant-induced palpitations — SALBUTAMOL (asthma), CAFFEINE, ALCOHOL (incl 'holiday-heart' AF + withdrawal), KHAT/miraa (a sympathomimetic stimulant used in parts of the region), DECONGESTANTS, EXCESS THYROXINE. The specific drug/stimulant history (salbutamol, khat, thyroxine, decongestants) is NOT cleanly tokenised ('caffeine/stimulants' + 'alcohol' are partial) — recommend a medication/stimulant field. Usually benign + reversible on stopping.
weights.weightCitation: Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022) (drug/stimulant-induced palpitations)

weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL on diabetes/insulin-sulfonylurea. ADRENERGIC palpitations (with tremor, sweating [not tokenised], hunger, anxiety) from hypoglycaemia — in diabetics on INSULIN/SULFONYLUREA, and in Uganda also from malaria/sepsis/alcohol/liver failure. DEFG — the glucose VALUE is the trigger but is NOT tokenised for this complaint (recommend a glucose check). Give glucose.
weights.weightCitation: ADA Standards of Care 2024; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022) (adrenergic symptoms of hypoglycaemia)

weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL on cardiomyopathy/HIV/pregnancy. Groups PERIPARTUM cardiomyopathy (late pregnancy/early postpartum — an obstetric must-not-miss, a leading cause of maternal cardiac death), HIV-associated cardiomyopathy, and dilated cardiomyopathy — all cause arrhythmia (AF/VT) + heart failure. Per the sexPrior caution: NO large fixed female delta (grouped entry — HIV/dilated affect both sexes); relies on the risk tokens, with a small OLDER-age penalty for the peripartum component so it is not mis-ranked for post-menopausal women. Echo; treat HF + arrhythmia.
weights.weightCitation: ESC cardiomyopathy guidelines; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022) (peripartum / HIV / dilated cardiomyopathy)

weights.csoNote: Palpitations as awareness of PAUSES/dropped beats or a slow pulse — bradyarrhythmia/HEART BLOCK. COMPLETE (3rd-degree) heart block causes syncope (Stokes-Adams) and SUDDEN DEATH and needs PACING — the must-not-miss within this entry, though it more often presents as syncope (see the syncope pack). Causes: conduction-system fibrosis, ischaemia, drugs (beta-blockers/digoxin/CCB — not tokenised). Rate/rhythm in vitals; ECG diagnostic.
weights.weightCitation: ESC 2021 Cardiac Pacing & CRT Guideline; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022) (heart block / bradyarrhythmia)

weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL on VTE risk. PE commonly causes SINUS TACHYCARDIA (the commonest ECG finding) or new AF, and can present with palpitations + dyspnoea + pleuritic chest pain +/- syncope +/- DVT. Pinned on prior VTE / recent immobility-surgery / cancer / pregnancy. (CANCER now wired as a risk + pin — it resolves via the 'cancer (specify site)' picklist, matching the dyspnoea PE entry.) Wells score + D-dimer/CTPA.
weights.weightCitation: ESC 2019 Pulmonary Embolism Guideline (Konstantinides SV et al.); Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022)

weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL on family history sudden death — RARE but critical. Congenital long-QT/channelopathy -> TORSADES -> syncope (esp on exertion/emotion/startle) and SUDDEN DEATH, classically in a YOUNG person with a FAMILY HISTORY of sudden/unexplained death or drowning. ACQUIRED long-QT (QT-prolonging drugs + hypokalaemia/hypomagnesaemia — links to the electrolyte entry) also causes torsades. Measure QTc on ECG; avoid QT-prolonging drugs; correct K/Mg.
weights.weightCitation: ESC 2022 Ventricular Arrhythmias Guideline; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022) (long-QT / channelopathy, torsades)
